text: You are on a motorway and see a sign: 'FOG'. What should you do?

options.text: Switch on dipped headlights, reduce speed, and increase following distance
Maintain speed — the sign is advisory only

explanation: In fog, use dipped headlights, reduce speed, and increase your following distance. Rear fog lights are permitted when visibility is below 100m.

text: When can you use a mobile phone on a motorway?

options.text: Only when queuing at less than 5 mph
Only in a service area after switching off the engine — never while driving or on the hard shoulder
When stationary on the hard shoulder waiting for breakdown recovery
Only in an emergency on the hard shoulder

explanation: You may only legally use a mobile phone when the vehicle is parked in a safe place with the engine off. Hard shoulder use is not permitted.

text: What is the maximum speed limit for a goods vehicle over 7.5 tonnes on a motorway?
explanation: Goods vehicles over 7.5 tonnes are limited to 60 mph on motorways and dual carriageways.

text: At night on a motorway you see a flashing amber light on the central reservation. What does this warn?

options.text: Road maintenance work or a hazard on the central reservation
Your vehicle's speed has exceeded the limit

explanation: Flashing amber lights on the central reservation warn of road maintenance, hazards, or emergency work. Slow down and proceed with caution.

text: What is the legal minimum tread depth for car tyres in the UK?
explanation: Car tyres must have at least 1.6 mm tread depth across the central three-quarters of the width, around the full circumference.

text: You check your engine oil and find it is at the minimum mark. What should you do?

options.text: Top up the oil before driving further
Add water to dilute the oil

explanation: Engine oil at minimum requires topping up before driving. Insufficient oil can cause severe engine damage very quickly.

text: Your brake fluid level is below the minimum. What does this indicate?

options.text: Normal evaporation — top up and continue
Possible brake pad wear or a leak — have it checked immediately

explanation: Low brake fluid can indicate worn brake pads or a brake fluid leak. Both require immediate professional inspection.

text: What is the purpose of anti-lock brakes (ABS)?

options.text: To brake faster than conventional brakes
To prevent wheel lock-up, allowing you to steer while braking hard
To automatically apply brakes in an emergency

explanation: ABS prevents wheel lock-up under heavy braking, allowing the driver to maintain steering control and follow a curved path.

text: How often should you check your tyre pressure?

options.text: Once a year at MOT time
At least once a week including the spare
At least once a month when cold, and before long journeys
Only when a tyre looks low

explanation: Tyre pressures should be checked monthly and before long journeys. Always check when cold (driven less than 2 miles).

text: You are about to drive in snowy conditions. Why must you clear all snow from your roof?

options.text: Snow can slide onto your windscreen or fly off and injure following drivers
Snow adds weight to the vehicle
It is a legal requirement to remove all exterior snow

explanation: Snow can slide off at speed and smash into the windscreen of the car behind, or onto your own. Clear it before moving.

text: What colour is the warning light for engine coolant temperature on most dashboards?
explanation: The coolant temperature warning light is red. If it comes on, stop safely as soon as possible — overheating causes serious damage.

text: You want to check your vehicle's engine oil level. When is the best time?

options.text: When the engine has been off for at least five minutes on level ground
Before starting the engine every morning

explanation: For an accurate dipstick reading, the engine should be off for several minutes so oil settles, on a level surface.

text: Your power steering suddenly fails while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Continue driving — steer harder, then have it checked
Switch the engine off and on

explanation: Power steering failure does not make the car unsteerable — it just requires much more effort. Slow carefully and get it inspected.

text: What does the tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS) light indicate?

options.text: One or more tyres is significantly under-inflated
Increase tyre pressure in all tyres

explanation: TPMS alerts you when a tyre drops 25% or more below recommended pressure. Stop safely and check the tyre(s).

text: Your car battery warning light illuminates while driving. What does this indicate?

options.text: The alternator is not charging the battery — a charging fault

explanation: The battery warning light means the alternator is not charging the battery. The car runs on battery alone and will eventually stop.

text: How should you test your brakes after driving through a deep ford?

options.text: Apply light brake pressure while driving slowly to dry them and check they work
Do not apply brakes until they dry naturally

explanation: After a ford, apply gentle braking to generate heat that dries the discs and pads and to verify the brakes are working correctly.

text: What does a flashing amber triangle warning light typically indicate?

options.text: A fault with the hazard light circuit

explanation: A flashing amber triangle usually shows traction control or electronic stability system has activated — it is working to prevent wheel slip.

text: Before a long winter journey, which checks are most important?

options.text: Antifreeze level, screen wash concentration, tyre pressures, lights, and oil

explanation: Winter checks: antifreeze, winter screenwash mix, tyre pressures (cold affects these), all lights, and oil level.

text: Your headlights are not working and it is dark. What should you do?

options.text: Use rear fog lights as an alternative
Park safely and do not drive until repaired

explanation: Driving without headlights in darkness is illegal and dangerous. Park safely and arrange repair before continuing.

text: What is the legal requirement for a car's horn?

options.text: Must work — only used when moving to warn others
Must sound for at least two seconds
Must be fitted but need not work

explanation: The horn must work and may only be used when moving to warn others. Using it while stationary or in frustration is illegal.

text: You notice oil on the ground where your car was parked. What should you check?

options.text: Engine oil level and look for signs of an oil leak

explanation: Oil on the ground suggests a leak. Check the oil level and look for the leak source. Do not drive until identified.

text: When should the check engine (engine management) light cause immediate concern?

options.text: If it comes on during a cold start
If it comes on and stays on while driving — it indicates an engine fault
If it flashes for a few seconds then goes out
Only if accompanied by unusual noises

explanation: The engine management light (amber) coming on and staying on indicates a fault. Have it diagnosed promptly. A flashing light means a serious misfire — slow down immediately.

text: You are checking your brake pads. What minimum thickness should they be?

options.text: At least 3 mm across the full surface
The disc must still be visible through the caliper window
There is no legal minimum — only advisory

explanation: Brake pads should have at least 3 mm of friction material remaining. Below this the stopping distance increases and the material may overheat.

text: Why is it important to check your mirrors before braking?

options.text: To see if the road behind is clear before reversing
So you know if a close-following vehicle needs more warning — brake progressively
To check your brake lights are working
Mirrors do not need checking before braking

explanation: If a vehicle is following closely, a gradual increase in brake pressure gives the driver behind time to react. Checking mirrors first is part of the MSM routine.

text: What is the speed limit in a built-up area unless signs say otherwise?
explanation: The default speed limit in a built-up area (with street lighting) is 30 mph unless signs indicate otherwise.

text: You are driving at night on an unlit road. When must you use headlights?

options.text: Only when visibility is less than 50 metres
Only when other vehicles are present

explanation: Headlights must be used between sunset and sunrise on all roads.

text: What does a double solid white centre line mean when the solid line is on your side?

options.text: Overtaking is prohibited — do not cross or straddle
Both vehicles must stay in their lanes

explanation: When the solid white line is on your side you must not overtake. You may cross only to enter premises or avoid an obstruction.

text: At a junction with traffic lights showing green, pedestrians are crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Wait for pedestrians to clear the crossing

explanation: Even when traffic lights are green you must give way to pedestrians who are already crossing the road you are turning into.

text: What is the purpose of the yellow box junction?

options.text: To mark a bus stop waiting area
To keep the junction clear of vehicles that cannot clear it
To mark a pedestrian crossing area

explanation: A yellow box junction must be kept clear. Only enter if your exit is clear — exception: you may wait when turning right if only oncoming traffic stops you.

text: What is the maximum speed limit on a single carriageway outside a built-up area for a car?
explanation: The national speed limit on a single-carriageway road outside a built-up area is 60 mph for cars and motorcycles.

text: You are driving along and the central line changes from broken white to solid white. What should this tell you?

options.text: You are approaching a national speed limit zone
You are entering a built-up area

explanation: A solid central white line indicates hazardous conditions making overtaking dangerous. Do not cross or straddle it.

text: What must you do before reversing into a side road?

options.text: Check all around for pedestrians, cyclists, and other traffic

explanation: Before reversing, check all around — use mirrors and look over your shoulder. Alert for pedestrians and cyclists.

text: When are you allowed to park on a clearway?

options.text: For quickly dropping off a passenger

explanation: A clearway (red cross on blue with red diagonal) means no stopping at any time. Includes parking, waiting, and setting down.

text: What is the rule about using a hand-held mobile phone while driving?

options.text: Prohibited at all times when driving, including at traffic lights

explanation: Using a hand-held phone while driving is illegal at all times including when stationary at lights. Penalty: £200 and 6 penalty points.

text: You are approaching a hump-back bridge with limited visibility. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain speed
Slow down — there may be oncoming vehicles hidden by the arch

explanation: Hump-back bridges restrict sightlines. Slow right down as a vehicle may be approaching from the opposite side unseen.

text: When should you use front fog lights?

options.text: Only when visibility is seriously reduced — less than 100 metres

explanation: Front fog lights may only be used in seriously reduced visibility of less than 100 metres. Other times can dazzle drivers.

text: At a toucan crossing, who may cross when the green figure shows?
explanation: A toucan crossing ('two can cross') allows both pedestrians and cyclists to cross simultaneously.

text: What is the maximum fine for driving without a valid MOT certificate?
explanation: Driving a vehicle that requires an MOT without a valid certificate carries a maximum fine of £1,000.

text: Traffic lights show red and amber together. What does this mean?

options.text: Prepare to stop — green was showing
Prepare to go — green is about to show
Stop — a fault has been detected

explanation: Red and amber together means the lights are about to change to green. Get ready to move but do not go until green.

text: You are driving on the left of a one-way street and want to turn right at the end. What should you do?

options.text: Remain on the left until the junction
Move to the right-hand lane in good time
Signal right from the left lane
It is illegal to turn right from a one-way street

explanation: On a one-way street, move to the lane appropriate for your exit in good time — right lane for a right turn.

text: What documents must you produce if asked by a police officer?

options.text: Driving licence, insurance certificate, and MOT certificate

explanation: You must produce a driving licence, insurance certificate, and MOT certificate. If not available, you have 7 days to produce them at a police station.

text: You are overtaking a cyclist on a rural road. How much space should you leave?

options.text: As much as you can — 0.5 m is enough in a narrow lane

explanation: The Highway Code (Rule 163) requires at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists at speeds up to 30 mph, and more at higher speeds.

text: A pedestrian who is blind and using a white cane is crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn gently to warn them
Stop and give way — do not move until they are safely across

explanation: Give blind or visually impaired pedestrians full priority. Stop well before them and remain still until they have safely crossed.

text: What is the minimum age to supervise a learner driver?

options.text: 21 years old, held a full licence for at least 2 years
21 years old, held a full licence for at least 3 years
18 years old, held a licence for at least 1 year

explanation: A supervisor must be at least 21 years old and have held a full UK or EU driving licence for at least 3 years.

text: What colour are temporary road-marking lines used in roadworks?
explanation: Temporary road markings in roadworks are yellow. They override white permanent markings and must be followed.

text: Chevron boards in roadworks indicate:

options.text: An obstruction — steer in the direction of the chevrons
A temporary speed limit has ended

explanation: Yellow-and-black chevron boards warn of an obstruction. Always steer in the direction the chevrons point.

text: A sign at roadworks shows a red triangle with the word 'SIGNAL'. What does this mean?

options.text: A manual stop/go controller is ahead
Emergency vehicle signals are in use

explanation: This warns of temporary traffic signals ahead. You must obey them as you would permanent traffic signals.

text: What is the speed limit in most motorway roadworks unless otherwise signed?
explanation: The mandatory speed limit in most motorway roadworks is 50 mph — enforced by average speed cameras.

text: You see temporary traffic lights in roadworks but they do not change after a long wait. What should you do?

options.text: Drive through carefully on red after checking
Continue waiting — they are controlled and will change

explanation: Temporary traffic lights may have long cycles. Wait patiently — never cross a red light even if the wait seems long.

text: Why are average speed cameras used in motorway roadworks?

options.text: To catch speeding at a single point
To enforce the speed limit over a stretch of road — making speeding throughout the zone pointless
To photograph plates for congestion charges

explanation: Average speed cameras record entry and exit times over a known distance. Speeding anywhere in the zone means prosecution.

text: Road workers are present in a motorway roadworks zone. What must you do?

options.text: Maintain normal motorway speed — they are behind barriers
Slow to the indicated speed limit and increase attention
Move to the middle lane only

explanation: Even with barriers, roadworks zones are dangerous for workers. Obey the limit, stay alert, and be ready for lane closures.

text: At a 'stop/go' board in roadworks, the board turns to 'go'. What should you do?

options.text: Check it is safe before moving — oncoming vehicles may still be clearing
Put on hazard lights and move slowly

explanation: Even when the board shows 'go', check it is safe before moving. Oncoming vehicles may still be in the single-lane section.

text: When should you merge into the remaining lane when a lane is closed with cones?

options.text: As early as possible when you first see the cones
At the merge point — zip merge one vehicle alternately from each lane
When you see the first sign
There is no rule — first come, first served

explanation: The zip merge uses both lanes up to the merge point, then drivers alternate. Early merging creates longer queues.

text: Cones close the hard shoulder on a motorway. Can you use it in an emergency?

options.text: Only if the cones are not solid
No — use the next emergency refuge area
Only if the vehicle is broken down

explanation: When cones close the hard shoulder in roadworks, it is part of the construction zone and off limits. Find the next ERA.

text: What is the fine for driving at 60 mph in a 50 mph roadworks zone?

options.text: Fixed penalty of £100 and 3 penalty points (up to unlimited fine via court)

explanation: A fixed penalty is £100 plus 3 penalty points. Court prosecution for high speeds can result in unlimited fines.

text: In roadworks, a sign shows a man digging. What does this warn?

options.text: Road surface is uneven or excavated — drive carefully
A temporary car park is ahead

explanation: The 'men at work' sign warns of road works, excavations, or road surface disturbances. Expect uneven surfaces.

text: Why are contraflow lanes used in some motorway roadworks?

options.text: To keep both directions of traffic moving on one carriageway
To allow road workers to work on the central reservation
To create a temporary overtaking lane
To route traffic via a diversion

explanation: A contraflow keeps both directions moving by routing them onto one carriageway, separated by cones.

text: How should you behave driving past road workers with no safety barrier?

options.text: Maintain speed — slow vehicles cause accidents
Slow down significantly and prepare to stop if a worker steps out
Sound your horn to warn them

explanation: Without a safety barrier, road workers are at extreme risk. Reduce speed significantly and be ready to stop at any moment.

text: You see a sign showing a 50 mph limit with a camera symbol in a roadworks zone. What does this tell you?

options.text: The limit is advisory near speed cameras
The average speed between cameras is monitored — stay at or below 50 mph throughout
Only the first camera enforces the limit
Speed is monitored only during working hours

explanation: Average speed cameras monitor your speed throughout the entire zone. You must maintain 50 mph or below throughout.

text: You arrive at the scene of a crash. A casualty is unconscious but breathing. What should you do?

options.text: Try to move them to a safer area
Place them in the recovery position unless a spinal injury is suspected
Remove their helmet if wearing one

explanation: An unconscious but breathing casualty should be placed in the recovery position to keep the airway open.

text: You witness a serious road accident. The first priority is to:

options.text: Try to pull casualties from vehicles

explanation: Make the scene safe first — warn approaching traffic and call 999. Rushing to casualties without making the scene safe creates more victims.

text: A motorcyclist is unconscious after a crash. Should you remove their helmet?

options.text: Yes — always to check for injuries
Only remove it if there is a breathing obstruction you cannot otherwise clear
No — never remove a crash helmet
Yes — but only a trained first-aider should do it

explanation: Remove a crash helmet only if the casualty's airway is obstructed and cannot be cleared otherwise. Unnecessary removal risks spinal injury.

text: If a casualty is not breathing, what should you do (having called 999)?

options.text: Place in the recovery position and wait
Begin CPR — 30 compressions then 2 rescue breaths
Apply tight bandages to all limbs

explanation: If not breathing, start CPR immediately: 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. Continue until help arrives.

text: What information must you give at the scene of a collision involving injury to another person?

options.text: Name, address, and vehicle registration number
Name, address, vehicle registration, and insurance details

explanation: If your vehicle is involved in an accident causing injury, give your name, address, vehicle registration, and insurance details to anyone with reasonable grounds to ask.

text: How should you control severe bleeding from a wound?

options.text: Apply firm direct pressure with a cloth or bandage
Wash the wound and apply antiseptic
Elevate the limb only — do not apply pressure

explanation: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or bandage. Maintain pressure and raise the limb if no bone is broken.

text: You are first on the scene of an accident involving a vehicle on fire. What should you do first?

options.text: Move casualties away from the vehicle if safe
Open the fuel cap to release pressure
Leave the scene and call from a distance

explanation: The priority is to move casualties away from the burning vehicle if it is safe to do so. Fuel tank fires can lead to explosion.

text: At the scene of an accident with a petrol spill, what should you warn against?

options.text: Anyone smoking or using a naked flame

explanation: Petrol vapour is highly flammable. Warn everyone not to smoke or use a naked flame, which could ignite the vapour.

text: What is the purpose of a warning triangle at an accident scene?

options.text: To light the scene at night
To warn approaching drivers of the hazard ahead, giving them more time to slow
To mark the vehicle position for insurance

explanation: A warning triangle placed at least 45 metres behind the scene gives approaching drivers advance warning to slow and take precautions.

text: You are involved in an accident. Your vehicle is still driveable. You must inform your insurance company:

options.text: Only if you were at fault
Only if another party makes a claim
As soon as reasonably possible after the accident

explanation: You must notify your insurer of any accident regardless of fault. Most policies require this within a short period.

text: What does FAST stand for in relation to stroke recognition?
explanation: FAST: Face (drooping?), Arms (can both be raised?), Speech (slurred?), Time (call 999 immediately). A stroke is a medical emergency.

text: A casualty is in shock after a crash. How should you position them?

options.text: Lying down, legs raised if no injuries prevent it, and keep warm

explanation: For shock: lie down, raise legs (if no injury prevents it) to improve blood flow, and keep warm. Do not give food or drink.

text: What is the danger of moving a casualty with a suspected spinal injury?

options.text: Permanently paralysing them by worsening spinal cord damage
Causing them to go into shock

explanation: Incorrectly moving someone with a spinal injury can compress or sever the spinal cord, causing permanent paralysis.

text: A child needs CPR. How does the technique differ from adult CPR?

options.text: It is the same — 30:2 compressions to breaths
Children receive 5 initial rescue breaths, then a 15:2 compression-to-breath ratio
Children receive only rescue breaths — no compressions
Children receive 30:2 but with softer compressions only

explanation: Paediatric CPR starts with 5 rescue breaths, then 15:2 compressions to breaths. Adult compression-only CPR is not recommended for children.

text: What information should you record at the scene of any accident for insurance purposes?

options.text: Name of the other driver only
Names, addresses, vehicle registrations, insurance details, witness contacts, photos of the scene and vehicles
Only photographs — details are collected by police
Nothing — wait for the insurance company to investigate

explanation: Record all details: parties' names and addresses, vehicle registrations, insurance companies, witness names, and photographs.

text: Which driving technique helps reduce fuel consumption the most?

options.text: Driving in a low gear at high revs
Anticipating traffic and driving smoothly at appropriate speeds
Keeping windows open instead of air conditioning
Using cruise control at all times

explanation: Smooth, anticipatory driving — avoiding unnecessary acceleration and heavy braking — is the biggest factor in reducing fuel consumption.

text: What effect does harsh acceleration have on fuel consumption?

options.text: None — fuel use is only affected by speed
It significantly increases fuel consumption and CO2 emissions
It reduces fuel consumption by shortening journey time
It improves fuel economy by warming the engine faster

explanation: Harsh acceleration burns much more fuel than gradual acceleration. Every unnecessary acceleration followed by braking wastes energy.

text: How does tyre pressure affect fuel consumption?

options.text: Correct pressure reduces rolling resistance and improves fuel economy
Under-inflation improves economy by increasing grip

explanation: Under-inflated tyres have greater rolling resistance. The engine works harder and uses more fuel. Correct pressure saves fuel.

text: What is the main greenhouse gas emitted by internal combustion engines?
explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the primary greenhouse gas from vehicle exhaust. It is the main vehicle contribution to climate change.

text: At what speed is fuel efficiency generally best for most modern cars on a motorway?
explanation: Most modern cars achieve best fuel efficiency at around 55–60 mph. Aerodynamic drag rises sharply above 60 mph.

text: Which vehicle contributes most to air pollution in urban areas?
explanation: Diesel vehicles in urban stop-start conditions produce high levels of NOx and particulate matter (PM2.5) — major urban pollutants.

text: How can you reduce your vehicle's CO2 emissions when buying a new car?

options.text: Choose a vehicle with higher engine capacity
Choose a vehicle with a lower CO2 rating (g/km)
Choose a heavier vehicle for stability

explanation: A lower CO2 rating means the car emits less CO2 per kilometre. It also typically means lower fuel bills and lower road tax.

text: What is the benefit of engine stop-start systems in urban driving?

options.text: They increase engine power at traffic lights
They reduce fuel consumption and emissions by switching the engine off when stationary
They extend engine life by reducing thermal cycles
They maintain battery charge more effectively

explanation: Stop-start systems switch the engine off when stationary and restart it instantly. This saves fuel and cuts emissions in urban driving.

text: What does a vehicle's Euro emission standard indicate?

options.text: The maximum permitted exhaust pollutant emissions

explanation: Euro standards (1 to 6+) define maximum permitted emissions of NOx, CO, and particulate matter. Higher numbers mean fewer emissions.

text: What is the environmental impact of unnecessarily idling your engine while parked?

options.text: None — idling consumes very little fuel
It produces emissions without useful movement, wasting fuel and polluting the local area
It helps the engine warm up and is beneficial

explanation: Idling produces CO2, CO, and NOx with no transportation benefit. Switch off the engine if stationary for more than a minute.

text: A catalytic converter reduces which pollutants?
explanation: A three-way catalytic converter converts CO, unburnt hydrocarbons (HC), and NOx into less harmful CO2, H2O, and N2.

text: What driving behaviour saves the most fuel on a long motorway journey?

options.text: Using the highest gear at the lowest safe speed
Maintaining 80 mph slightly above the limit
Switching off the engine on downhill sections

explanation: Driving in the highest suitable gear at a moderate steady speed reduces engine revs and fuel consumption significantly.

text: What is the environmental advantage of car sharing?

options.text: Reduced per-person emissions — fewer vehicles make the same journey

explanation: Car sharing reduces the number of vehicles on the road. Two people sharing one car halves the per-person CO2 for that journey.

text: How does regular vehicle servicing help the environment?

options.text: It has no environmental benefit — servicing is only for reliability
A well-maintained engine burns fuel more efficiently and produces fewer emissions
Only electric vehicles benefit from servicing

explanation: A regularly serviced engine — clean air filter, fresh oil, correct spark plugs — operates efficiently, consuming less fuel and emitting fewer gases.

text: What is one environmental benefit of driving in a higher gear at lower revs?

options.text: Lower fuel consumption and reduced CO2 emissions

explanation: Higher gear at lower revs means the engine is working at its most efficient point, reducing fuel use and CO2 emissions significantly.
